vid_urls.title: U.S. Spacewalk 97
vid_urls.description:
At approximately 8:35 a.m. EDT (1235 UTC) on Aug. 18, 2026, NASA astronaut Anil Menon and ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot will venture outside the International Space Station for an approximately six-and-a-half-hour spacewalk. The pair will replace a Space-to-Ground antenna that enables high-speed communications between the Mission Control Center in Houston and the orbital complex. 

This spacewalk will be Menon’s second and Adenot’s first. Adenot will become the first French woman to conduct a spacewalk.

Learn more about this spacewalk: https://go.nasa.gov/4x9ASdi
Read the latest mission updates from the station: https://nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/

Credit: NASA

info_urls.title: Join ESA for a total solar eclipse on 12 August 2026
info_urls.description: Follow the total solar eclipse with the European Space Agency (ESA), in person or online.

vid_urls.title: 2026 Total Solar Eclipse
vid_urls.description:
Come watch the eclipse with NASA.

On Wednesday, Aug. 12, a total solar eclipse will be visible in parts of Greenland, Iceland, Spain, and the Atlantic Ocean. A partial solar eclipse will be visible in most of Europe and parts of North America.

Totality will begin in Iceland at 1:45 p.m. EDT (1745 UTC) and in Spain at 2:28 p.m. EDT (1828 UTC).

Can't see it where you are? We'll be streaming live views from a number of cameras in the path of the eclipse — and sharing info about the science of eclipses and how we're studying them.

More info on our live coverage: https://go.nasa.gov/3TvNDAd
Learn more about eclipses: https://science.nasa.gov/eclipses/

vid_urls.title: Total solar eclipse 2026: Coming to Europe (Official ESA broadcast)
vid_urls.description:
Watch live with us as a total solar eclipse becomes visible across parts of Europe on 12 August 2026.
 
The path of totality will sweep across Greenland, Iceland, Spain and a small area of northeastern Portugal, while much of Europe will experience a partial eclipse.
 
A total solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes directly between Earth and the Sun, completely blocking the face of the Sun.
 
Join us live from the Observatorio Astrofísico de Javalambre in Spain, a world-class astronomical observatory located within the path of totality, where scientists, astronomers and special guests will explore the science behind eclipses, the Sun and their wider relevance for space science and Earth.

vid_urls.title: The 12 August 2026 Total Solar Eclipse: online observation.
vid_urls.description:
More here: https://www.virtualtelescope.eu/

Next 12 August, the Sun will amaze us with a stunning total eclipse. We will bring the show to you live.

This 12 August, the Sun will offer a stunning total eclipse, visible from Europe. The Virtual Telescope Project will bring to you the stunning beauty of such a unique event, covering it both from Manciano, Italy, where it will be partial, and from Spain, where it will be total.

We thank the Exploratorium - San Francisco for making possible for us to share their imagery of totality from Spain.

The online, free total solar  eclipse session is scheduled for 12 August 2026, staring at 17:30 UTC.
